subject: Service-level metrics & auditor access — procurement questionnaire
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@nimbus-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement questionnaire: service-level metrics and auditor access

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking our procurement questionnaire. A few items on SLOs/SLAs we need clarified for our internal security and procurement review:

1) Measurement windows: What rolling window do you use to compute availability/latency (30d, 7d, other)?
2) Latency definition: For text-generation APIs, do you measure server-side request-to-last-token, or do you include network egress/streaming time? Which percentiles are reported (p50/p95/p99)?
3) Monitoring and alerts: What stack do you use (Prometheus/Grafana, internal), and can we receive read-only dashboards or prometheus remote_write for our monitoring?
4) Incident metrics: How do you classify incidents vs. transient errors; what is the process for validating downtime for SLA credits?
5) Auditor access: For our auditors, can you provide read-only access to historical metrics and raw traces for a specified period (12 months)? If not full access, what evidence packages do you provide?

If you can answer briefly and attach samples (SLO definitions or screenshot of the dashboard), we can move this through the procurement team.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Procurement Lead
Nimbus Analytics

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire: service-level metrics and auditor access

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. See answers below and attached artifacts (SLO excerpt + sample dashboard). I'm happy to hop on a quick call if you'd like to walk through anything.

Summary answers (high level):
- Measurement windows: rolling 30-day and 7-day windows for reporting; 90-day aggregated view for trend analysis. SLA eligibility is evaluated on a 30-day rolling window.
- Latency definition: we report server-side time-to-last-token (server processing + model decoding). We surface client-observed latency in the console for troubleshooting but do not include end-user network egress in SLA metrics. Reported percentiles: p50, p95, p99 (and p999 for internal ops).
- Monitoring & alerts: primary stack is Prometheus + Grafana on our internal monitoring cluster; all SLOs are computed using Prometheus recording rules and exported to Grafana dashboards. We also push alerts to PagerDuty and to the Redwood Console alerts pane.
- Incident classification: We differentiate between degraded (increased error rate/latency) and outage (complete service unavailability) using predefined thresholds; each incident is post-mortemed and linked to the SLO calculation window to determine SLA impact.
- Auditor access & evidence: We can provide three options: 1) read-only Grafana links to time-bound dashboards; 2) a snapshot evidence package (metric exports, incident timelines, and evaluation reports) suitable for auditors; 3) for enterprise contracts, a controlled prometheus remote_write or S3-delivered metric export for a negotiated period.

Operational details and caveats:
- Maintenance windows: we honor scheduled maintenance with a 48-hour advance notice and they are excluded from SLA calculations if declared and communicated in advance. For ad-hoc maintenance that affects customers, we treat on a case-by-case basis and provide credits per contract terms.
- Custom monitoring: For Dedicated/Private customers we offer read-only Grafana and can set up prometheus remote_write on request (subject to security review).
- Alerts: Customers can subscribe to customer-facing alerts via the Console (email/Slack/Webhook). Internal ops alerts (PagerDuty) are part of our escalation path but not shared unless on an agreed integration.

See attachments: redwood_slo_definitions.pdf (SLO language + measurement rules), service_metrics_dashboard.png (sample Grafana dashboard), redwood_sla_excerpt.docx (example SLA excerpt showing credit calculations).

Next steps: let me know which evidence option your auditors prefer and whether Nimbus requires prometheus remote_write or read-only dashboards. If you want a formal exception path (for e.g., extended maintenance windows or custom SLO measurement), we have a DocuSign template that we use for negotiated terms.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Technical Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Torres <elena@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nimbus-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire: service-level metrics and auditor access

Hannah — this is very helpful, thank you. A couple of clarifying items from procurement/security: 

- For the rolling windows, can you confirm whether the 30-day window is calendar-based or a trailing 30 days recalculated daily? We need trailing 30-day for our scoring.
- For incident validation: what evidence do you accept to trigger an SLA credit (incident ticket + postmortem + metric slice?) and how long after an incident do we have to request credits?
- For auditor access: our auditors will require read-only access to dashboards and metric exports for a 12-month period during their review window. Will you permit a time-limited Grafana account for auditors (SAML/SCIM provisioning preferred)?

Also: Nimbus wants a clause that allows a one-off SLA evaluation exception if we can demonstrate a correlated outage on our side (e.g., network provider) that materially affected our observed metrics. Do you have a standard exception request form/process?

If you can confirm these lines and, if possible, provide a sample post-incident evidence bundle, we can attach it to our procurement workbook and move to legal review.

Thanks,
Elena

Subject: Fwd: Procurement questionnaire: service-level metrics and auditor access

Elena — forwarding with additional notes from our compliance & SRE teams.

Connor: adding the SRE perspective on evidence bundles.

Elena — quick answers from compliance/SRE: 
- Trailing window: the 30-day rolling window is trailing and recomputed daily (yes).
- Evidence bundle for SLA credit requests: we accept the incident ticket ID, the postmortem document, metric slices (Prometheus query extracts for the impacted period), and a validated incident timeline. Requests for credits must be submitted within 30 days of the incident close (standard), though commercial terms can extend this in negotiated agreements.
- Auditor access: we support time-limited read-only Grafana (SAML/SO provisioning) for enterprise customers. Onboarding is via our security intake form; auditors receive time-bound accounts scoped to the requested dashboards.
- Exception process: we have an SLA Exception Request form (DocuSign link below) — customers fill the form attaching supporting evidence (network provider outage, third-party maintenance notices, etc.). Exceptions are reviewed by our Ops & Legal teams and responses are provided within 10 business days.

Links & artifacts: 
- DocuSign SLA Exception template: https://www.docusign.com/templates/custom-sla-nimbus
- Sample evidence bundle (redacted): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3cSLO-Definitions

If that covers it, we can send a formal addendum that specifies the auditor account provisioning flow and the evidence checklist.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Manager, Compliance & Controls
Redwood Inference
